title: Thermodynamics of the $q$-deformed Kittel--Shore model for spin-1 particles
abstract: Quantum algebras ($q$-algebras) have been used in the literature to deform spin-chain models. In particular, in previous works by the present authors, the Kittel--Shore Hamiltonian was deformed using $\mathfrak{su}_q(2)$ algebra. The deformed Hamiltonian was presented for a general spin, and the thermodynamic properties were studied for spin-1/2 particles. In this paper, we focus on the $q$-deformation of the Kittel--Shore model for spin-1 systems. We analyse the impact of this deformation on the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of the system as a function of the deformation parameter $q$. Specifically, we study the specific heat, magnetic susceptibility, and magnetisation, including a detailed analysis of the Curie temperature characterising the ferromagnetic phase. Furthermore, a finite-size scaling analysis is conducted for both the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic cases. Results are systematically compared with those of the undeformed model to reveal the physical effects of the $q$-deformation.
summary: This work studies the thermodynamics of the Kittel–Shore model for spin-1 systems after applying a $q$-deformation derived from quantum algebras. The authors calculate key observables like specific heat and susceptibility, finding that the deformation significantly alters the system's energy spectrum and phase transition behavior compared to the standard model. This research connects quantum group theory to the statistical mechanics of quantum magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum algebra deformation affects the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of the Kittel–Shore model for spin-1 particles.
main_result: The $q$-deformation significantly alters the thermodynamic functions, causing shifts in energy profiles and breaking the universal scaling behavior observed in the undeformed model.
method: The analysis involves calculating the partition function and deriving thermodynamic observables (specific heat, susceptibility, magnetization) for the $q$-deformed Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is the Kittel–Shore (KS) model applied to spin-1 particles, whose Hamiltonian is deformed using the $U_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ quantum algebra.
key_observables: Specific heat ($C_V$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), magnetization ($M$), and the Curie temperature.
important_parameters: Deformation parameter ($q$ or $\eta$), spin value ($j=1$), interaction constant ($I$), and external magnetic field ($h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results in the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$) against finite-size scaling results, and uses low-temperature approximations in some parts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy levels and degeneracies for $j=1$ as a function of the deformation parameter $\eta$, and show the density of energy levels $D(E)$ for various system sizes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the model by first presenting the undeformed case, then examining the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic regimes separately, and finally conducting finite-size scaling analyses for both.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how algebraic deformations (quantum groups) can modify fundamental thermodynamic quantities in condensed matter models, offering insights into how microscopic symmetries affect macroscopic phase transitions.
